candidates.title: Reward Errors Change Memory Before They Change Policy
candidates.one_sentence_thesis: A terminal label is a write-time state-update treatment: it robustly changes durable memory text, but source-faithful retrieval usually attenuates the success/failure distinction before branch-specific policy uptake, so forced sensitivity is not realized transport.
candidates.missing_scientific_object: A stage-resolved causal decomposition of write -> exposure -> branch-specific uptake -> outcome for reward-conditioned persistent memory.
candidates.core_insight: The scientific object is not whether feedback can shape memory; it is where a controlled label intervention survives or attenuates along the persistent-state transport path.
load_bearing_chain: same experience, label-only writer intervention -> 20/20 durable state divergence
stronger same-mode wording reduction -> reward semantics survives generic prompt explanation
forced swap -> latent conditional leverage exists
exact retrieval -> exposure is measurable and can be broad
native S/F first-action probe -> branch-specific uptake is weak before terminal scoring
native terminal + raw + neutral structured controls -> broad practically-large branch-specific transport is not established
candidates.closest_work_boundary: ReasoningBank/Reflexion/AttriMem already establish feedback-conditioned or learned memory construction; this story claims stage-resolved identification and attenuation of a label-only state intervention, not a new memory architecture or feedback-learning method.
candidates.negative_evidence_role: Native non-passes are load-bearing localization evidence rather than failed replications.

candidates.title: Your Evaluator Is Also a State Updater
candidates.one_sentence_thesis: When terminal feedback selects a persistent-memory writer, evaluator error is no longer only a scoring error because it can modify durable state that future decisions may retrieve.
candidates.missing_scientific_object: Evaluator reliability after the score is consumed by persistent-state updates.
candidates.core_insight: A judge can be operationally consequential even without parameter updates because its label changes memory construction.
candidates.closest_work_boundary: Strong practical framing but higher collision risk with JudgeBench/RewardBench and Memory Reward Inflation unless the stage-resolved transport decomposition remains explicit.
candidates.negative_evidence_role: Native attenuation narrows the safety/reliability consequence rather than supporting a broad harm claim.

candidates.title: Memory Intervention Sensitivity Is Not Memory Transport
candidates.one_sentence_thesis: A persistent state can change outcomes under forced injection while producing little effect under the released retrieval/interface path, so intervention sensitivity and realized transport must be evaluated separately.
candidates.missing_scientific_object: A methodological separation between forced state intervention and source-faithful persistent-state transport.
candidates.core_insight: The same memory pair can be causally potent under injection yet behaviorally inert under native exposure and uptake.
candidates.closest_work_boundary: Very clean evaluation lesson, but it underuses the novel byte-identical reward-conditioned write intervention and risks reading as a benchmark/protocol paper.

winner.reason: It preserves the strongest novelty boundary (label-only write intervention), uses B10/B11 negative evidence as mechanism localization rather than embarrassment, and gives the causal-mechanism archetype an explicit mediator path from durable state to policy uptake to outcome.
final_story_spine: Scene: self-evolving agents convert self-judged outcomes into reusable persistent memory.
Stake: a wrong label can become state, but text corruption matters only if it survives retrieval and policy uptake.
Current paradigm: success/failure-conditioned or reward-trained memory construction is established prior art.
Failure mode: the same byte-identical experience can be committed through a different reflection objective when the terminal bit is wrong.
Missing object: stage-resolved survival of a label-only intervention across write -> exposure -> branch-specific uptake -> outcome.
Identification: 20/20 write divergence beyond a stronger wording reduction.
Latent leverage: forced injection passes a terminal practical-effect gate.
Exposure: exact released retrieval can be broad after bank expansion.
Uptake bottleneck: native S/F first-action TV and modal action changes are weak.
Outcome boundary: native S/F, raw, no-memory, outcome-blind structured, and denser-endpoint controls do not establish a broad practically-large branch-specific effect.

Bounded conclusion: evaluator reliability is a persistent-state reliability issue, but downstream risk requires stage-resolved transport auditing rather than inference from memory-text divergence alone.

additional_experiment_adjudication.question: Would an outcome-blind structured-memory first-action arm materially change the winning story?
additional_experiment_adjudication.reason: The paper's causal treatment is success-vs-failure label switching. B10 already measures this exact treatment at first-action uptake, while B11 controls generic structured rewriting at the downstream endpoint. A neutral first-action arm would mainly estimate generic structured-memory presence relative to outcome-conditioned writers, which is outside the current narrow claim and would not be required to establish branch-specific attenuation.
additional_experiment_adjudication.reopen_condition: Run B12 only if the manuscript expands its claim to generic structured-memory presence, outcome-conditioned-writer semantics independent of label direction, or a formal mediation claim requiring the neutral arm at the same process endpoint.
